USMLE-style practice · Pharmacology

Redistribution after a bolus

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A highly lipid-soluble intravenous anesthetic causes rapid unconsciousness after one bolus. The patient awakens as the drug moves from the brain to other tissues, before most of the dose has been eliminated. Which process primarily explains this early recovery?

  1. Immediate irreversible receptor destruction
  2. Failure of the IV dose to reach circulation
  3. New synthesis of all plasma proteins
  4. Redistribution
  5. Complete renal elimination within seconds
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Redistribution

Movement away from the brain can terminate a single-bolus effect before metabolic elimination is complete.

Understanding the options

Redistribution
Movement away from the brain can terminate a single-bolus effect before metabolic elimination is complete.
Complete renal elimination within seconds
The stem states that most of the dose remains in the body.
Immediate irreversible receptor destruction
This would not explain normal recovery.
Failure of the IV dose to reach circulation
The rapid onset shows systemic and brain delivery.
New synthesis of all plasma proteins
This is not the rapid process described.
